negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring alone will systematically miss foreign-PSP hiring and leadership signals; English-language and third-party channels are mandatory complements for this half of the cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's six seeded actors are only a fraction of HU-licensed payment and e-money institutions. Smaller PSPs, e-money issuers, PISP/AISP third-party providers and BNPL/wallet players were not enumerated in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive the full population from the MNB Intézménykereső (pénzforgalmi intézmény + elektronikuspénz-kibocsátó intézmény categories) cross-referenced with the HUNFINTECH member list and the HUNFINTECH 20/20 ranking, then attach an employer-site monitor per entity.

coverage_gaps.description: No direct feed of statutory officer changes (Cégközlöny / e-cégjegyzék, the official company gazette and registry) was located or tested in this pass; only commercial aggregators (Nemzeti Cégtár, OPTEN) were found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate the official Cégközlöny/e-cégjegyzék publication channel for changes to vezető tisztségviselők at the tracked entities — it is the legally authoritative, PR-independent leadership-change signal.

coverage_gaps.description: The strongest quantitative hiring signals (LinkedIn HU job counts, Glassdoor review flow) sit behind ToS that forbid automated collection, and the two most useful first-party career sites (Revolut, Wise) are JS-rendered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for either a licensed job-postings data provider or a headless-browser collector for the ATS endpoints of Barion, Wise and Revolut; treat profession.hu as the compliant HU-language fallback after a robots/ToS check.

coverage_gaps.description: Named role-holders gathered here (SimplePay, Revolut HU, PayU HU, Barion officers) are drawn from media and aggregator snapshots of varying dates and are not point-in-time verified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a role-holder register keyed to entity + role with a source and as-of date per assertion, refreshed against the first-party leadership page and the registry, so stale appointments are visibly stale rather than silently wrong.

coverage_gaps.description: Sector events (FinTechShow, Internet Hungary) surfaced only incidentally. Speaker rosters and award shortlists are a systematic census of who currently holds which role, but no event-source monitoring was set up.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the FinTechShow and Internet Hungary agenda/speaker pages as recurring annual pulls and diff speaker affiliations year over year.

brief: Hungarian payments employers split cleanly into two source regimes. Domestic players (SimplePay/ex-OTP Mobil, Barion) publish in Hungarian on their own sites — SimplePay maintains a vezetőség page and a dated press stream that carried both its Kft.-to-Zrt. conversion and its CEO appointment, while Barion offers a careers portal but no discoverable press room, so its officer changes must be read from the company registry. Foreign players (Revolut, Wise, PayU) have almost no Hungarian-language first-party surface: their signals arrive via English careers sites, HU business media (Forbes.hu broke the Revolut country-lead appointment; Portfolio and FinTechZone tag streams aggregate the rest), and press wires like Prim. The reliable backbone for this cell is therefore regulatory and registry data — the MNB Intézménykereső for the true employer population and Nemzeti Cégtár/OPTEN for PR-independent officer changes — with media and career sites layered on for timeliness; the main constraints are ToS-blocked hiring-volume sources (LinkedIn, Glassdoor) and JS-rendered ATS pages.
